## Objective

Establish that the current instructions yield the requested results, then tie the evidence to all eight requirements.

## Scope

- Disposable ordinary-prompt trials, skill and ownership checks, and a final requirement and preservation audit.

## Entry conditions

- The applicable root and Template versions, their tests and their local authority bindings have been identified. The ordinary-prompt fixtures are independent of managed Tasks.

## Exit criteria

- The three ordinary-prompt checks report attributable outcomes. Handoff format, ownership and stopping results are reviewable.
- Every criterion has current evidence or a precise outstanding result. Completion requires passing current evidence for every required criterion and a final, strictly later inspection of all protected paths.

## Risks

- A static phrase match cannot demonstrate user-visible behavior. Retain the actual outputs and compare them to the observable acceptance criteria. A few cases support only case-specific claims.

## TASK-008 - Run the three ordinary-prompt trials

In clean, disposable local contexts that load the installed instructions, give an agent each of the three ordinary user requests without coaching it on the acceptance criteria. Retain the actual final output and the relevant actions and observations for each case.

### Risks

- Coaching the response or using a static text match would mask the handoff behavior under test. A missing document must not be simulated with an accessible substitute.

### Acceptance criteria

- The agent finds the single documented command, runs it without a clarification turn and reports the observed result.
- The agent reproduces a failing check, identifies the recoverable cause, fixes it and reruns that same check successfully.
- With one of two named sources absent, the agent gives the supported finding, identifies the exact unsupported conclusion and asks only for the missing input. The three trials create no managed Task.

### Planned verification

- Provide a release bundle and one documented check command. Record the command chosen, exit status, checked artifact and any questions asked.
- Give the repair prompt and its failing fixture, record the original failure, attributable edit, identical rerun and resulting output.
- Provide only one of two named records. Compare each factual conclusion with the accessible record, read the final reply alone and compare read-only Task inventories across the ordinary trials.

## TASK-009 - Check output formats and ownership boundaries

### Risks

- A passing prose review cannot attest to a runtime action. Identify the evidence type for each result and preserve artifact-only output exactly.

### Acceptance criteria

- Advice is usable as delivered. A material assumed detail is disclosed where the format allows. A fill-only request returns exactly its expected artifact and preserves the protected wording.
- For a consequential choice the agent asks the minimum resolving question, respects the applicable approval step and finishes independent work. An explicit stop ends work within its stated scope under the current ownership rules.
- An inspectable assignment example, bounded worker return and coordinator integration check exist. A specialist completes its own work and refers an adjacent item to the manager. Routine prompts leave the ledger untouched.

### Planned verification

- Compare the advice with the actual request and compare the fill-only output byte for byte with the supplied expected text.
- Use a disposable case with a consequential authorization choice and independent evidence. Record the question, supported result and actions after an explicit stop.
- Trace the example from assignment through the worker's evidence and the coordinator's direct check. Compare the specialist handoff with all three role pairs and inspect the Task inventory without changing it.

### Risks

- A historical run or a planned command can be mistaken for a current pass. Give each observed result its source, date, version and verification level.

### Acceptance criteria

- All eight requirements and all fifteen criteria have evidence at the required level. Each changed file and check has a scoped reason.
- The final response states the delivered result, supporting checks and any precise unmet criterion. It honors the requested output format and closes only after the remaining authorized work has been completed or accurately reported.

### Planned verification

- Compare every requirement, dependency and acceptance criterion with the phase results. Record the exact criterion and planned verification step addressed by each current evidence item.
- Reopen the final source, Template and depot files. Compare the scoped diff, products, historical records, registry, Task boundaries and unrelated working edits with their baseline. Before marking the plan complete, append a final project inspection dated strictly after the last task and requirement evidence, with a preservation result for each protected path.
- Read the final reply without the progress history and check that it makes only claims supported by the inspected files, commands or native trials.
